scareclaw-kashtira.verdict: The most complete deck in the collection: two opening engines, deep interaction (17 pieces), and an OTK going second.
scareclaw-kashtira.edge: 20 one-card starters (97.6% to open one) and 17 interaction pieces; it has the second-best odds in the collection of opening both a play and interaction (92.9%).
scareclaw-kashtira.risk: Scareclaw's zone-placement rules make the first Summon fragile, and Tri-Heart's Scareclaw-only lock punishes wrong sequencing.
nat: Day 2 contender
Strong on both sides of the die roll, which is what survives 9+ rounds. The ceiling is lower than the format's top Angelechy and Elfnote boards, so a top cut needs good pairings.
reg: Top 8 contender
Regional fields have fewer fully optimized meta builds, and Super Polymerization ×3 plus Kashtira banishes answer most of what shows up.
loc: Low brick risk and deep interaction make it the safest deck to bring to an unknown room.

branded-dracotail.verdict: The best mix of ceiling and consistency in the collection (9.0 and 8.5). Two Fusion engines rarely get stopped by a single hand trap.
branded-dracotail.edge: 18 one-card starters (96.0%), Quick-Effect Fusions on the opponent's turn, and six Mulcharmy draws going second.
branded-dracotail.risk: Heavy discard costs drain the hand in long games, and banish or GY hate hits both engines. Branded lost Albion and Branded Opening went to 1 on the Oct 19 list.
nat: Day 2 contender
Branded still put several decks in the YCS Houston top 32. The Dracotail engine adds resilience the stock lists don't have.
reg: Top 8 contender
It opens a full board almost every game, which is how most regionals are won.
loc: Very few local decks can stop two separate Fusion engines.

kashtira-maliss.verdict: A banish-loop Link deck with an unusually thick hand-trap suite. It's strong going first and holds up going second.
kashtira-maliss.edge: 13 hand traps plus Bystials, and the Kashtira package gives free bodies on an empty field.
kashtira-maliss.risk: Only one real going-second board breaker (Nibiru; 15% to see it in 6 cards), and the Link-only and Xyz-only locks need careful ordering.
nat: Day 2 bubble
Maliss reached the top 32 at YCS Columbus in May but not at Houston in October. It's playable at a national event, not a favorite.
reg: Top 16 contender
Its going-first board plus 13 hand traps is better than most regional fields.
loc: Consistent and interactive, though the complex sequencing makes misplays costly.

tenpai-wyrm.verdict: The biggest high roll in the collection: Swordsoul builds on the Main Phase, then Tenpai Synchros mid-Battle Phase for the kill.
tenpai-wyrm.edge: Ceiling 9.5. The Battle-Phase OTK can win going second through boards that Main-Phase decks can't break.
tenpai-wyrm.risk: Only 9 true starters (74.2%), four engines to sequence, and Sky Striker Engage is now Semi-Limited (this build already runs 2).
nat: Day 2 bubble
Sky Striker shells made YCS top cuts in 2026, and the OTK steals rounds. Execution difficulty is the limiting factor over a long event.
reg: Top 16 contender
The Battle-Phase kill punishes players who don't keep Battle-Phase interaction, which is common at regionals.
loc: Explosive enough to beat anyone, but the 25.8% chance of no one-card starter means some hands lose to themselves.

spright.verdict: A hand-trap-first deck: the best going-second deck in the collection, with a solid Level 2 combo when it goes first.
spright.edge: 20 interaction pieces and 11 board breakers. It's 87.6% to hold a breaker going second, the best in the collection.
spright.risk: The highest brick rate here (7.6%). With only 5 engine pieces, a hand without a starter rarely recovers, and the Dogmatika locks clash with Spright plays.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Spright is several formats old, and its end board is smaller than current Tier 1 decks. The going-second strength keeps it winning rounds.
reg: Top 32 possible
3 Nibiru and 3 Evenly Matched punish regional decks that commit everything to one board.
loc: A field of combo decks with few backrow answers is exactly where this deck thrives.

radiant-typhoon.verdict: Three independent engines (Radiant Typhoon, Angelechy and Albaz Fusion), and the most going-second breakers of the Angelechy pair.
radiant-typhoon.edge: Angelechy is the strongest engine left after the Oct 19 list (9 of the YCS Houston top 32), and Sky Striker Radiant Typhoon also made that top 32.
radiant-typhoon.risk: No Traps, only 10 one-card starters (78.3%), and Meghala's WIND-only lock blocks every Angelechy and Fusion play that turn.
nat: Day 2 contender
It shares the format's best surviving engine and has 7 breakers going second. A purer Angelechy list would still be favored over this hybrid.
reg: Top 8 contender
Its going-second suite (3 Droplet, 3 Super Poly, Nibiru) handles regional end boards well.
loc: Most local fields can't keep up with three engines plus going-second removal.

pieces: Radiant Typhoon Fonix, the Great Flame
Radiant Typhoon Varuroon, the Vibrant Vortex

dinomorphia-ryzeal.verdict: A Trap-lock control deck that spends Life Points as a resource. It's tied with Spright for the most interaction in the collection.
dinomorphia-ryzeal.edge: 94.8% to open a play plus interaction, the best here, and 90.9% to hold 2+ interaction going second. Rexterm's negation shuts down combo turns.
dinomorphia-ryzeal.risk: No going-second board breakers. It also keeps its own LP low, so burn or a single big attack can end it.
nat: Day 2 bubble
Rexterm locks out combo-heavy fields, which is most of the current format. Missing breakers costs rounds against established boards.
reg: Top 16 contender
Strong against regional combo decks that aren't prepared for Trap-based negation.
loc: Very hard to beat for players who don't side in backrow removal.

white-forest.verdict: A high-ceiling Synchro and Fusion combo deck where Super Polymerization doubles as an extender and a going-second answer.
white-forest.edge: Ceiling 9.0, with 15 starters and two engines (White Forest Synchro and Diabellstar).
white-forest.risk: The third-highest brick rate here (3.8%). The DARK Extra Deck lock and three competing Field Spells punish sequencing mistakes, and Azamina Ilia Silvia is now Forbidden.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
The Azamina hit removed part of its ceiling, and White Forest isn't a current national-level archetype. It can still take rounds off strong decks.
reg: Top 32 possible
When it opens well, its high-roll boards beat most regional decks.
loc: Its explosive turns outclass most local boards.

pieces: Elzette, Azamina of the White Forest

horus-mitsurugi.verdict: A grinding deck: GY recursion plus Ritual board wipes. It's very consistent but its interaction is thin.
horus-mitsurugi.edge: 1.0% brick rate, and Horus recursion is hard to remove for good.
horus-mitsurugi.risk: Only 11 interaction pieces, Rituals can be hit by Ash at several points, and several Extra Deck effects are dead text.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Horus and Mitsurugi pieces appeared in YCS Houston's Light and Darkness Ritual decks, but the Oct 19 list hit that shell. This standalone build lacks its power.
reg: Top 32 possible
Recursion wins long games against regional decks without banish effects.
loc: Few local decks can grind through repeated GY revivals.

earthbound-resonator.verdict: A Red Dragon Archfiend Synchro grind deck with a separate Horus engine as insurance.
earthbound-resonator.edge: Ceiling 8.5, and the Horus half builds a board even if the Resonator chain is stopped.
earthbound-resonator.risk: Resonator effects lock you to DARK Dragon Synchros, and GY hate shuts off most of both engines.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Neither Resonator nor RDA is a current national-level deck, and Necrovalley-style hate is common at that level.
reg: Top 64 possible
Good enough to win rounds, but the lock-heavy combo is easy to disrupt.
loc: The independent Horus engine is a real edge against local hand-trap counts.

ignister.verdict: A fast Cyberse Link combo with many one-card starters and a strong hand-trap suite.
ignister.edge: 17 starters (94.9%) and 14 interaction pieces, plus Ra Sphere Mode as an unusual going-second breaker.
ignister.risk: One of the lowest floors here: one interruption plus single copies of the WATER and WIND pieces makes recovery hard. A.I. Meet You's lock also blanks your own hand traps.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Not a current national-level archetype, and its recovery after a hand trap is poor.
reg: Top 64 possible
Its speed can beat opponents who don't keep hand traps.
loc: Consistent openers win many local rounds.

interaction: The Winged Dragon of Ra - Sphere Mode

blackwing-angelechy.verdict: A Blackwing Synchro swarm with Angelechy as a parallel value engine. It's explosive going first.
blackwing-angelechy.edge: Ceiling 8.5, and it shares the Angelechy engine that dominates the current format.
blackwing-angelechy.risk: Nibiru was cut, leaving few going-second answers (39.4% to see a breaker), and two different Extra Deck locks constrain its lines.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Angelechy is top tier, but the Blackwing half dilutes it. Players who want Angelechy at a national event play the pure version.
reg: Top 32 possible
Strong going first. Losing the die roll is its main risk.
loc: Its Synchro swarm overwhelms most local boards.

pieces: Blackwing - Vata the Emblem of Wandering

swordsoul-tenyi.verdict: A grinding control deck with deep interaction (tied for third-most) and the fewest true starters in the collection.
swordsoul-tenyi.edge: Floor 8.0, with 17 interaction pieces and 3 Evenly Matched. It wins long games.
swordsoul-tenyi.risk: Only 6 one-card starters (57.7%), so many hands need two engine cards, and its end board is small.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
The low ceiling can't keep up with current Tier 1 boards.
reg: Top 64 possible
Hand-trap density steals rounds against combo decks.
loc: Very hard to blow out, even if it rarely dominates.

primite-blue-eyes.verdict: A classic Blue-Eyes control deck with two engines that reach the same double-negate board.
primite-blue-eyes.edge: Strong going first (Spirit Dragon, Ultimate Spirit Dragon, Stardust Sifr) with 15 starters.
primite-blue-eyes.risk: Zero going-second board breakers. Behind a strong board, it relies on Tyrant Dragon and Drillbeam alone.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Without going-second breakers it loses too many rounds on the die roll.
reg: Top 64 possible
Its going-first board holds against regional decks, but its going-second games are weak.
loc: A board with multiple negates beats most local decks.

runick-typhoon.verdict: A floodgate control deck that wins by milling. It almost never bricks, but it can't break a board.
runick-typhoon.edge: 0% brick rate, and Inspector Boarder plus Dimensional Fissure lock out decks that use the Extra Deck or GY heavily.
runick-typhoon.risk: No board breakers, and its own Boarder limits Fonix. Opponents who play around Boarder's count or bring backrow removal beat it.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Floodgate decks get sided against heavily over a long event, and it has no way to break a board going second.
reg: Top 32 possible
Many regional players don't side in answers to Boarder or Fissure.
loc: Can lock out unprepared opponents completely.

pieces: Radiant Typhoon Fonix, the Great Flame

metalmorph-fiendsmith.verdict: A Max Metalmorph Trap toolbox designed to avoid dead draws. It's very consistent but has a thin hand-trap suite.
metalmorph-fiendsmith.edge: 0.6% brick rate, and its bosses come out at Trap speed, which avoids Extra Deck hate.
metalmorph-fiendsmith.risk: Only 12 interaction pieces and few going-second outs beyond Super Polymerization and Nibiru.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Not a meta deck, and its going-second games against strong boards are poor.
reg: Top 64 possible
Consistency carries it through weaker rounds.
loc: Its Trap-speed bosses surprise players who don't know the deck.

gren-maju.verdict: A layered floodgate lock with a scaling beater. It's devastating when it locks and helpless when it doesn't.
gren-maju.edge: Ceiling 9.0: Macro Cosmos, Necrovalley and Boarder together lock out GY decks almost completely.
gren-maju.risk: The lowest floor here (4.5). Its floodgates turn off its own cards, and it's weak going second.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Floodgate decks get sided against, and the current top decks have answers.
reg: Top 64 possible
It can win rounds outright against GY-dependent regional decks.
loc: Opponents unfamiliar with stacked floodgates often can't play at all.

pieces: Gizmek Orochi, the Serpentron Sky Slasher

ryu-ge-mitsurugi.verdict: A Level 10 Pendulum control deck plus a Mitsurugi Ritual engine. It has a high ceiling but few true starters.
ryu-ge-mitsurugi.edge: Ceiling 8.5, and two independent engines reach a wide Rank 10–12 toolbox.
ryu-ge-mitsurugi.risk: Only 8 starters (69.4%) and 6 interaction pieces, the fewest in the collection (65% to see one in 6 cards).
nat: Unlikely to top cut
A Mitsurugi deck reached the top cut at YCS Columbus in May, but this hybrid lacks the interaction for a long event.
reg: Top 64 possible
Its board wipes win rounds, but light interaction leaves it exposed.
loc: Board wipes and big bodies overwhelm many local decks.

synchron.verdict: A generic Synchron toolbox. It's flexible and consistent, but its ceiling is low and many of its effects lock it into Synchros.
synchron.edge: 0.7% brick rate and 16 starters. It almost always does something.
synchron.risk: Several dead-text effects and Synchro-only locks hold back its power.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Its end boards are too small for current Tier 1 decks.
reg: Top 64 possible
Consistency wins rounds against weaker decks.

lunalight.verdict: The Lunalight Fusion chain from Cat Dancer to Liger Dancer, with a deep hand-trap suite. Its combo is the least consistent in the collection.
lunalight.edge: Liger and Leo Dancer clear boards, and its 11 interaction pieces give it a real going-second plan.
lunalight.risk: The named-material Dancer chain and only two Fusion Spells make it the hardest combo here to assemble.
nat: Unlikely to top cut
Not a current national-level deck, and its combo is too fragile.
reg: Top 64 possible
Liger Dancer board wipes can steal games.
loc: Fun, and capable of big swing turns.
